chunks: Know that Al-Husayn ibn Said narrated from Hammad ibn Isa from Abdullah ibn Maymun from Abu Abdillah from his father, peace be upon them both, who said:

The Zakat al-Fitr is a Sa' of dates, or a Sa' of raisins, or a Sa' of barley, or a Sa' of aqit (dried curds), for every person, free or slave, young or old, and there is no hardship upon one who cannot find what to give in charity.

Ibn Qulawayh narrated from Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn Mas'ud from Ja'far ibn Ma'ruf who said: I wrote to Abu Bakr al-Razi regarding Zakat al-Fitr and asked him to write to our Master, meaning Ali ibn Muhammad (peace be upon him), regarding this matter. He wrote that this had been sent to Ali ibn Mahziyar: 'That it is to be given from every item—dates, wheat, and other than them—as a Sa'. And we have no difference of opinion regarding his answer to us on this matter.

key_terms.زَكَاةُ الْفِطْرَةِ: Zakat al-Fitr (the obligatory charity at the end of Ramadan)
key_terms.صَاعٌ: A Sa' (a traditional unit of volume measurement)

ai.seo_question: What are the specific food items and quantities required for Zakat al-Fitr in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* codifies the Fiqh of Zakat al-Fitr, establishing the Sa' measurement and validating diverse staple foods like raisins and aqit, a ruling confirmed by the letter of Imam Ali ibn Muhammad (al-Hadi). It underscores the universality of the obligation across all demographics while providing a practical exemption for the indigent, reflecting the Shia emphasis on accessible purification of the fasting person. The inclusion of the Imam's correspondence highlights the scholarly reliance on authoritative transmission chains to resolve minor variations in material application.
